bib.venue: book chapter (Statistical Rethinking, 1st ed. context; year not printed in the chapter extract)

question: How can multiple regression separate spurious association, masked relationships and multicollinearity, and what goes wrong when variables are added?
contributions: Spurious association via predictor residual, counterfactual and posterior prediction plots
Multicollinearity, post-treatment bias, categorical variables, OLS/lm correspondence

limits: Regression answers a descriptive question about the sample, not forecasting and not intervention (Summary p.162).
Causal inference depends on unverifiable assumptions (p.120).
Counterfactual plots can show impossible predictor combinations (p.131).
Collinearity simulation uses flat priors that exaggerate SD inflation (p.150).
Fits use quadratic approximation (map), not MCMC; the rethinking package and data(WaffleDivorce, milk, Howell1) are the author's; Chapter text has no year printed.
practices: Do not call multiple regression 'control'; avoid causal language (p.123).
Inspect results with predictor residual plots, counterfactual plots and posterior prediction plots (p.126).
Drop NA cases explicitly and know that lm/glm drop them silently (p.136).
Use log of body mass for scaling variables (p.137).
Check predictors with a pairs plot; correlations above about 0.9 are a warning, and diagnose by SD inflation when both enter (p.148).
Show that any one of a cluster of correlated variables gives same inferences (p.149).
Do not control for post-treatment variables if the goal is the causal effect of treatment; do control for pre-treatment variables (p.150-152).
Use k-1 dummies for k categories, or an index variable with one intercept per category (p.155,158).
Compute contrasts from posterior samples, never compare significance of two parameters (p.157-158).
Sum or subtract posterior samples, not interval boundaries, since parameters are correlated (p.154).
Prefer explicit as.factor and pre-transformed variables in lm; lm gives no sigma uncertainty (p.160-161).
